tidal.gear: Area 29 gear: barbless hooks only; one line in the tidal Fraser; no multi-point hooks Sep 1 – Mar 31; no finfish fishing from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise.

rules.licence: You need a BC freshwater fishing licence with the salmon conservation surcharge, and you must record retained adult chinook on your licence right away.
rules.hatchery: "Hatchery-marked" means the adipose fin has been clipped off, leaving a healed scar. See Salmon ID.
rules.disclaimer: This map is an unofficial aid. River lines come from OpenStreetMap and the ends of each stretch are approximate. The DFO wording and any fishery notice always take precedence.
guide.intro: In rivers most salmon are in spawning colours. These marks still work on bright ocean fish: gum colour and tail spots.
guide.hatchery.title: Hatchery-marked or wild?
guide.hatchery.body: A hatchery-marked salmon is missing its adipose fin, the small fleshy fin between the dorsal fin and the tail, and has a healed scar in its place. If the adipose fin is there, the fish is wild. Where a limit says "hatchery-marked", release wild fish.
fish.Chinook.m1: Black gums at the base of the lower teeth
fish.Chinook.m2: Large black spots on the back, dorsal fin and both lobes of the tail
fish.Chinook.m3: Spawners turn dark olive to bronze or maroon
fish.Coho.m1: White or grey gums with a dark mouth
fish.Coho.m2: Spots on the back and only the upper lobe of the tail
fish.Coho.m3: Spawning males turn bright red with a dark green back and a hooked jaw
fish.Chum.m1: No distinct black spots on the back or tail
fish.Chum.m2: Spawners show purple and green vertical "calico" bars
fish.Chum.m3: White tips on the pelvic and anal fins; males grow large canine-like teeth
fish.Pink.m1: Large oval black spots on the back and both tail lobes
fish.Pink.m3: Spawning males grow a tall hump. Southern BC runs come mainly in odd-numbered years
fish.Sockeye.m1: No large black spots on the back or tail
fish.Sockeye.m2: Spawners turn bright red with an olive-green head
fish.Sockeye.m3: Males develop a hooked jaw and a hump
